signals.quote: Additionally, Patagonia became a certified B Corp in 2011 and a California Benefit Corporation in 2012. Both designations require companies to include public benefit in their mission and ensure accountability to stakeholders.
signals.note: Patagonia has been a certified B Corp since 2011, which means it is committed to public benefit and accountability.

signals.quote: The company has set Science Based Targets Initiative-verified goals aligned with Paris Agreement warming thresholds: reducing Scope 1 and 2 emissions (from owned facilities and purchased electricity) by 80% and Scope 3 emissions (from materials, supply chains, and transportation) by 55% by 2030, compared to a 2017 baseline.
signals.note: Patagonia has set Science Based Targets to reduce its greenhouse gas emissions by 2030, which are verified and align with the Paris Agreement.

signals.quote: Unfortunately, the brand has yet to make progress toward reducing its emissions in line with its science-based targets. Between 2017 and 2025, Patagonia’s total, absolute emissions have increased by approximately 25%, from 145,848 metric tons of carbon dioxide equivalent (tCO2e) to 182,646 tCO2e (equivalent to around 21 million gallons of gasoline).
signals.note: Patagonia's total emissions increased by about 25% between 2017 and 2025, indicating it has not yet made progress toward its science-based targets.

signals.quote: Outdoorwear brand Patagonia uses lower-impact materials and traces most of its supply chain. Patagonia sustainability rating Planet 4 out of 5 People 4 out of 5 Animals 4 out of 5 Overall rating: Good
signals.note: Good On You rates Patagonia as 'Good' overall for its sustainability, with scores of 4 out of 5 for Planet, People, and Animals.

signals.quote: They hold an overall B impact score of 151 – which is about 3 times the average score of an ordinary business, and almost twice the minimum score to qualify as a Certified Benefit Corporation.
signals.note: Patagonia has a B Impact score of 151, which is significantly higher than the average business and well above the minimum for B Corp certification.

signals.quote: Ranking in the top three leading global companies were Nike, BrewDog and H&M, all of which had under 100,000 metric tonnes of greenhouse gas emissions per year. However, of the three, BrewDog is the only company with a B Corp certification.
signals.note: H&M does not have a B Corp certification, unlike some other companies on a list of eco-conscious brands.

signals.quote: Which fashion brands are certified as B - corporations: H&M & Zara Eileen Fisher & Patagonia Gucci & Armani All answers are correct Here’s the best way to solve it.
signals.note: H&M is not certified as a B-corporation.

signals.quote: Our climate targets have been validated by the Science Based Targets initiative (SBTi) , an independent organisation that assesses whether corporate emissions-reduction targets are aligned with climate science.
signals.note: H&M Group's climate targets have been validated by the Science Based Targets initiative.

signals.quote: In 2023, H&M Group reported a total of 8,586,805 ton CO₂e, and a net revenue of 22,258 M USD, resulting in a emissions intensity of 386 t CO₂e / M USD.
signals.note: H&M Group reported its total greenhouse gas emissions for 2023.

signals.quote: Based on all publicly available information we’ve reviewed, we rate H&M “It's a Start” overall.
signals.note: Good On You rates H&M as 'It's a Start' overall for sustainability.

signals.quote: H&M Norway has been called out for “greenwashing” following an investigation into its Conscious Collection conducted by the Norwegian Consumer Authority (CA) .
signals.note: The Norwegian Consumer Authority criticized H&M for potentially misleading marketing of its Conscious Collection.

signals.quote: Back in 2019 Norway’s Forbrukertilsynet (Consumer Authority) revealed that they were investigating fast fashion giant H&M’s sustainability claims.
signals.note: Norway's Consumer Authority investigated H&M's sustainability claims for its Conscious Collection.
